thread:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] spike in 5xx errors — eu3-gateway service. error-rate > 7% over 2m, latency p95 ~ 2.3s. Pager escalation to #incidents. :rotating_light:
Alex Chen: I'm on it. pulling logs from eu3 gateway now. any customer reports?
Maria Gonzalez: seeing elevated 502s on dashboards; a few API customers showing retries. tagging support to surface any hit customers. @Jenny Wu can you check the biggest callers?
Jenny Wu: support says 3 enterprise customers reported timeouts over last 10m, mostly tokenization calls. escalating their internal tickets.
Sanjay Patel: sharing quick metrics:
```
cpu_util eu3-gw: 78%
connection errors: 1.2k/min
upstream 5xx: spike from 00:10 -> 00:18
```
Sanjay Patel: tcp dumps show many half-open connections to model-proxy replicas in eu3. gatekeeper circuit-breaker tripped on 3 nodes.
Alex Chen: circuit-breaker tripped -> traffic diverted to regional fallback (eu2) which is now seeing a surge and increased latency. might be a cascading routing loop.
Ryan Baker: is autoscaling for eu3 model-proxy healthy?
Sanjay Patel: ASG scaled but cooldown was long; replicas in Pending for ~3m. suspected Docker image pull delay from internal registry.
Alex Chen: OK, mitigation options: 1) Pause circuit-breakers to stop double-failover (risk increased error spread), 2) Force route-shift to us-east-1 for heavy customers, 3) Restart model-proxy fleet in eu3 after draining.
Maria Gonzalez: recommend route-shift for critical customers while we restore eu3. less blast radius.
Jenny Wu: agreed. I'll ask Customer Success to notify the 3 affected customers about temporary routing to us-east-1.
Alex Chen: executing weighted routing change: increase weight us-east-1 for route /v1/generate -> 70% (eu3 -> 30%). running the command now:
```
# set routing weights
rdctl route update --route /v1/generate --weights eu3=30,us-east-1=70 --reason "evacuate eu3 due to proxy failures"
```
IncidentBot: deploy-bot: Routing update submitted, change id 82f9. Rollout starting.
Ryan Baker: I'm patching the image-pull issue on registry edge; will reduce pull latency.
Sanjay Patel: starting rolling restart on eu3 model-proxy with drain mode: 2 pods at a time. running drain script:
```
kubectl annotate pod <pod> cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true
kubectl rollout restart deploy/model-proxy -n eu3 --max-unavailable=2
```
Alex Chen: watch logs for reconnect errors. If circuit-breaker remains tripped after restarts, we may need to reset counters from CB admin.
Maria Gonzalez: customer-facing SLOs: error-rate impacting ~3% of requests globally during the peak. notifying SRE lead and product.
Jenny Wu: CS notified customers; they accepted route-shift for now. sending canned message: "We've temporarily routed traffic to our alternate region while we fix eu3; no data was lost."
Sanjay Patel: after 8min of restarts, pods are healthy, connection backlog cleared. circuit-breaker counters still in tripped state on 1 node.
Alex Chen: manual reset on CB for node gw-03: `cbctl reset gw-03 --force` — doing it.
IncidentBot: cbctl: reset accepted for gw-03.
Alex Chen: monitoring. error-rate falling: now 1.1% in eu3 and 0.8% globally.
Ryan Baker: registry fix deployed, image pulls down to 150ms from ~2.8s. autoscaler no longer stuck.
Maria Gonzalez: suggestion: add fallback cooldown of 60s before routing weight change to prevent churn. filing jira: INF-3219.
Jenny Wu: summarizing customer impact for postmortem: 3 enterprise customers saw timeouts for ~12m, mitigated by routing to us-east-1, no data loss, repro steps filed.
Alex Chen: ok, rolling back weighted route: restoring eu3 to 85% after verifying stability. command:
```
rdctl route update --route /v1/generate --weights eu3=85,us-east-1=15 --reason "restore eu3 after recovery"
```
IncidentBot: routing change id 82fa applied.
Sanjay Patel: all eu3 nodes now healthy, p95 latency down to 120ms.
Alex Chen: lowering incident severity to SEV-3. preparing handoff. oncall window ends in 15m.
Maria Gonzalez: creating incident report draft and assigning action items: registry resiliency, fallback cooldown, better CB metrics.
Jenny Wu: Customer Success will follow-up with affected customers with RCA and timeline.
Oncall Pager: Handoff: Alex -> Ryan for next shift at 01:00 UTC. Ryan, you're now oncall for followups and postmortem.
Ryan Baker: acknowledged. I'll keep watching for any routing thrash and follow up on INF-3219 items.
Alex Chen: final notes: detection threshold needs tuning — we should avoid CB flips during registry slowness. tagging infra and runtime teams. good job team. :thumbsup:
